newsitem.title: USA: US administration to reform IRS - Treasury's Summers.
newsitem.headline: US administration to reform IRS - Treasury's Summers.

text.p: Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Monday that it was time to modernize the Internal Revenue Service to make it more responsive to U.S. taxpayers.
In a speech before the Tax Executives Institute, Summers outlined a series of measures that the Clinton administration will work toward implementing.
A consensus had emerged, he said, among congressional leaders, union members, business executives and others that "it is time for change."

Summers unveiled a five-point plan that will focus on "oversight, flexibility, budgeting, tax simplification and leadership." He said that as a first step the Treasury would devote necessary resources, both managerial and financial, to strengthen itself and become more "pro-active" in its oversight of the IRS.
Secondly, the plan would "enhance and strengthen" the IRS's ability to manage its operations so that it is not tied down by bureaucratic red tape in taking measures it feels are necessary.
In addition, Summers said the administration would work with Congress to help the IRS get the stable and predictable funding it needs to operate more effectively.
"Today, the IRS operates in a low-trust, short-tether budgeting environment," he told the meeting.
"This makes rational planning for capital projects such as information technology very difficult," he added.
In addition, Summers said the administration would work to simplify the tax code but said it remained opposed to "extreme measures such as a flat tax."

Lastly, the administration is committed to appointing a new commissioner with experience in "organizational change, customer service improvement and information technology management that the IRS faces."
